name: Puppet Animation
visualIdentity: Articulated figures with identifiable materials, stable costumes, and miniature sets. Pose for visible weight, balance, and foot contact; identify whether puppets are physically photographed or digitally rigged. Avoid rubbery deformation, costume flicker, and intersecting joints.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to character drama; suggested for whimsical narratives, theatrical brand stories, education, and story chapters. Symmetric frontal staging and brief notes can support clear poses. Interactive HTML can use scene selectors, still frames, descriptions, and keyboard navigation. Suitability beyond these examples is inferred.
limitations: No intrinsic palette or required cadence is specified. Digital rigs are simulations, not physical puppet photography. Do not impose stop-motion stepping solely from the style name. Flat images cannot support unseen views or arbitrary camera orbits; preserve projection, grounding, and readable labels. Omit gaze-following without suitable eyes, layers, or a rig.
palette: Resolve colors from task, approved brand or reference, and existing semantic mappings first. The optional three-token example for new presentation elements only is background #EDE4D1, foreground #414638, accent #8E8263; it does not define puppet colors. Preserve costumes, sets, source art, exact colors, color families, and color-count limits. No gradients; accent is decorative, not body text. Check actual composited contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Pose motion to preserve weight, balance, and foot contact; held replacement poses are allowed but not mandatory. For video, derive states from seekable time and verify direct and reverse seeks. Interactive HTML may use bounded pointer gaze or miniature-scene parallax when assets support them; scroll can drive angle-linked annotations, chapter handoffs, or story steps. Keep pupil motion anatomical, layers grounded, and transitions reversible. Orbit needs complete 3D geometry or enough turntable views; a single flat image cannot reveal unseen sides. Use patterns only when scene-supported.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied choices and assets. Synchronize picture and sound, leave speech intelligible, avoid clipping, and inspect them together.
assetRequirements: Physical production needs poseable puppets, miniature sets, consistent framing, and photographed frames. Digital alternative: Blender rigs with held keyframes, clearly labeled as simulated. Preserve alpha, dimensions, and frame naming for prepared layers or sequences. Gaze needs facial layers or a suitable rig; parallax needs separated depth layers or true 3D; orbit needs complete geometry or sufficient captured views. Do not imply missing assets or physical production.
combinations: Suggested: frontal axial symmetry (style-104) for theatrical staging, with camera moves lateral or axial and feet grounded; avoid handheld drift and recoloring costumes. Suggested: held-shot annotations (style-024) for education or chapters; brief notes in #414638 with #8E8263 accents, never over faces or during action. These are optional, and the actual costume/set palette governs. Motion overlays such as gaze, parallax, or chaptered storytelling need scene-specific asset and geometry checks.
productionApproach: Choose visual construction and motion tools for the style and assets before the export framework. Physical route: pose and photograph puppets frame by frame. Digital route: Blender rigs and held keyframes, distinguished from photography. Python may prepare assets; FFmpeg may encode sequences and combine audio. HyperFrames is the default for seekable assembly, sync, validation, and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output, recording why. Keep rendering and motion logic separate from the pipeline; use deterministic time, inspect key frames and the decoded video, and deliver editable source, contact sheet, parameters, and render instructions.
